title: Get your first useful result
objective: Judge a suggestion against practical constraints and justify a tool choice.
explanation: You decide what a useful result means. A fluent suggestion can still miss your time, budget, or audience. Write down the constraints, compare the suggestion with them, and change or reject it. You can do this with a person, a checklist, or an AI tool. Choosing not to use AI is a valid outcome; the goal is a decision you can explain.
scenario: Fictional club brief: six students have 10 minutes, no spending money and no phones. A draft suggests a paid online tournament lasting 45 minutes.

activities.prompt: Which revision fits all three constraints?

choices.text: Keep the tournament but call it quick.
choices.feedback: A new label does not change the cost, phones, or duration.

choices.text: Run a 10-minute paper word game using scrap paper.
choices.feedback: This fits time, cost, and device constraints; check that everyone can participate.

activities.rationale: Compare the actual plan with every stated constraint.

activities.prompt: What is a defensible way to choose your tool?

choices.text: Use AI because newer tools are always better.
choices.feedback: Novelty is not evidence of usefulness.

choices.text: Use a checklist or ask the club; use AI only if it adds something worth checking.
choices.feedback: Either a non-AI or AI-supported route can work when you explain the fit.

choices.text: Let the tool choose without reviewing it.
choices.feedback: You remain responsible for whether the plan works.

activities.rationale: Credit justified non-use equally with justified use.

transfer.prompt: Changed constraint: the club now has only FIVE minutes. Six students, no spending and no phones still apply. Adapt your original plan: give a new time allocation including setup and clearing away, explain what you cut or kept, reconsider your tool choice, and name an inclusion check and a role to consult. Use fictional details.
rubric: The revised times total no more than five minutes, including setup and clearing away.
Explains what changed from the original attempt and why; still no spending or phones.
Justifies keeping or changing the tool choice, including non-use.
Names an inclusion check and a role to consult without personal details.

uncertainty: A proposed activity is not proven successful until tried with its actual participants.

optionalMedia.description: No media needed. Use the written scenario and choices.

branchActivity.prompt: What should guide a revised plan?

choices.feedback: Excitement does not resolve the constraint mismatch.

choices.text: The actual time, cost and device limits.
choices.feedback: Use the stated limits to evaluate the plan.

branchActivity.rationale: Complete this short check, then return to the main lesson.

completionPolicy.requires: All visible required core/branch choices and required text fields

responseFields.prompt: Your first attempt: write a 10-minute plan for the six students before seeing the example. Include time, cost, devices and your tool choice.
criteria: Include setup and clearing away in 10 minutes.
Use no spending and no phones.
Explain a tool choice or justified non-use.

responseFields.prompt: Self-review: name one criterion your revised plan meets, show the detail that supports it, and identify one uncertainty to check.
criteria: Point to evidence in your own plan.
Name a remaining uncertainty without claiming the activity has been tested.

teaching.question: What makes a suggestion worth using?

sections.title: Start with what success needs
sections.text: For the fictional club, success means six students can join an activity within 10 minutes, with no spending and no phones. Those are constraints: conditions the result must satisfy. An exciting description does not make a plan fit.

sections.title: Inspect the draft, one condition at a time
sections.text: The proposed online tournament takes 45 minutes, costs money and needs phones. It fails all three checks. You do not need an AI tool to notice this. Put the brief beside the suggestion and mark each mismatch.

sections.title: Repair it, then check what you missed
sections.text: A possible repair uses one minute to explain a scrap-paper word game, seven minutes to play and two minutes to share. That totals 10 minutes and needs no spending or phones. It is still a proposal: ask the club organizer whether everyone can read, write or contribute another way.

practice.title: Start with your own plan
instructions: Write a first plan before opening the worked example. Include setup, activity and clearing away in 10 minutes.
Check no spending and no phones. Choose a tool or explain why none is needed.
Keep this first version for comparison; you will adapt it to a changed constraint later.
practice.selfCheck: Is every constraint visible in your plan? What still needs checking with the club organizer?

teaching.takeaway: Define useful → check every constraint → revise or reject → explain your decision.
teaching.independentPractice: Tomorrow, try the same three-constraint check on a fictional plan without reopening the worked example. Explain one reason to use a tool and one reason not to.
